levels.title: Not adopted
levels.summary: Nothing here enforces a standard yet

levels.title: Configured
levels.summary: The enforcing package is installed, so the checks can run

levels.title: Reporting
levels.summary: The check runs in the repository's own CI and publishes what it found

levels.title: Current
levels.summary: On the current release, owned, and readable by AI tooling

signals.title: Installs the standards package
signals.detail: composer.json requires newfold-labs/wp-php-standards, for artifact types that have a PHP standard. Types with no PHP standard yet satisfy this trivially rather than failing a check that does not exist for them.

signals.title: Pins the standards package
signals.detail: The declared constraint names a version rather than floating. @stable, * and branch aliases install whatever is newest whenever composer update runs, which admits the current release and so reads as maximally up-to-date while being the least predictable thing in the fleet. Rolling a change out as a version bump rather than an overnight CI failure is the point of pinning, so it is measured separately.

signals.title: Pinned to the current release
signals.detail: The declared constraint admits the latest release of the package. A constraint that cannot reach the current version is what stops a repository from ever running a newly added rule, so it is the signal that gates the top of the ladder.

signals.title: Reports compliance from its own CI
signals.detail: The repository has uploaded a standards-compliance artifact. This is the definition of adoption: the sweep never runs a linter itself, so a repository that does not report is one we have no findings for.

signals.title: No findings at error severity
signals.detail: Nothing at error severity that cites a documented standard. Raw phpcs severity is not the gate: the inherited sniffs carry the severities WPCS ships, where a missing docblock is an error and a security finding is a warning, so gating on those would hold repositories off this rung against a policy we did not write. Findings without a rule are still reported, they just do not decide a level.
signals.read: reported findings, or the central scan

signals.title: Has an owner
signals.detail: CODEOWNERS exists and is not empty. A row nobody owns is a row nobody fixes, which is why ownership is a level and not a footnote.

signals.title: Carries AI context
signals.detail: AGENTS.md exists, so AI tooling working in the repository can reach the standards rather than guessing at them.

rules.title: Names entering the global namespace carry a company prefix
Nonces are verified, output is escaped and input is sanitized
